title: A Preregistered Audit of Dataset Contamination Controls in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory audit to measure the prevalence and operational effect of dataset-contamination flags in selected public LLM-for-NetOps benchmark items. Using a frozen plan (study: contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1), we evaluated 150 item pairs (baseline vs guarded) with a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a deterministic generate–validate procedure and a formal netops validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Preregistered contamination detectors (exact-match + fuzzy 5-gram overlap + provenance timestamp heuristics) produced no high-confidence contamination flags in the executed items; consequently no guarded-condition exclusions/replacements occurred. All 150 baseline episodes and their matched guarded episodes passed the functional validator (baseline = 150/150, guarded = 150/150). The preregistered paired test (exact McNemar two-sided) yields estimate = 0.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.0–0.0), p = 1.0. We report this null confirmatory outcome, diagnose the causes (no high-confidence flags; shared initial generation semantics per preregistration), and discuss what the result does and does not imply about contamination risk in LLM‑for‑NetOps evaluations. Key limitations include a single-model run, synthetic task sources in the executed sample, and design choices (shared-initial candidates) that constrained sensitivity to some contamination scenarios. We provide the frozen preregistration identifier and execution artifacts for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Motivation — Generative models are being proposed for NetOps tasks (intent→configuration, repair) but reliable adoption requires understanding dataset contamination and evaluation-construct validity. Prior work shows LLMs can produce plausible network artifacts yet may hallucinate or exploit memorized templates; agentic generate–validate architectures reduce regressions (evidence: contemporary benchmarks and system papers). Research question — After preregistering a contamination-detection and realism-adjustment protocol, how prevalent are high-confidence contamination flags in a sampled set of public NetOps benchmark items, and how does applying preregistered contamination controls affect measured model success rates? Contributions — (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory design executed end-to-end with stored artifacts (study contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1); (2) exact, reproducible confirmatory outcome statistics (Npairs=150); (3) a failure-mode diagnosis showing why the experiment returned a null effect and prescriptive guidance for stronger future audits.
sections.related_work: Surveyed empirical and systems literature shows (i) LLMs can translate intents into configuration artifacts in constrained tasks (fine-tuning or in‑context learning) and (ii) LLM-driven repair often introduces regressions that formal verification or iterative validate–repair loops can detect or reduce (Cornetto; Asadli et al.; Astragalus; Protogeros et al.). Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber-family, Minesweeper) serve as practical oracles for reachability/policy checks and were used conceptually to motivate the validator choice. Methodological literature highlights benchmark contamination and construct-validity risks for LLM evaluation and recommends evidence-bounded audits and provenance-aware detection; our experiment implements a preregistered subset of those recommendations.
sections.methodology: Preregistration — We froze the experimental plan and analysis (see preregistration id contamination-audit-netops-2026-v1; preregistration manifest hash recorded in the execution manifest). Design — paired binary confirmatory design comparing baseline vs guarded conditions on the same item set; planned 150 items sampled deterministically from the preregistered benchmark scope; model set: single hosted model gpt-5-mini; adapter/framework: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Generation semantics — the preregistration permitted shared_initial_candidate generation across conditions (independent_condition_generation=false); this was executed as specified. Contamination detection — deterministic exact-match fingerprinting (normalized token equality), fuzzy 5-gram overlap (Jaccard-style shingle overlap) with preregistered thresholds (high-confidence flag if exact-match OR 5-gram overlap ≥ 0.80), and provenance timestamp checks versus model cutoff. Guarded-treatment — preregistered rule: exclude high-confidence-flagged items and deterministically replace them by seeded retemplated + topology-augmented items that pass intent-preservation checks (embedding cosine ≥ 0.85) before execution. Validator — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implemented functional intent-preserving checks (final-state constraints, sequence constraints, and reachability/policy invariants) and produced binary pass/fail used as the episode outcome. Analysis — primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test McNemar exact two-sided with paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Missingness and failed-call rules and sensitivity analyses were preregistered and followed.
sections.results: Execution summary — planned episodes 300 (150 items × 2 conditions); completed episodes 300; model_calls_used 150 (shared-initial generation per item). Contamination flags — preregistered detectors produced no recorded high-confidence flags for the executed items (contamination_summary empty); thus the guarded treatment performed zero deterministic exclusions/replacements. Outcomes — baseline successes 150/150 (1.0), guarded successes 150/150 (1.0). Paired contingency (n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). Primary paired estimate = 0.0 percentage points; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. All preregistered artifacts (raw outputs, validator traces, manifests, analysis tables) are recorded in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion: Interpretation — The confirmatory test produced a precise null effect: no change in measured success after applying the preregistered guarded procedure. Two nonexclusive operational causes explain this outcome: (1) the sampled items did not trigger high-confidence contamination flags under the preregistered heuristics, and (2) the preregistered shared_initial_candidate generation (independent_condition_generation=false) produced identical model outputs for baseline and guarded episodes, limiting the design's capacity to detect differences absent exclusions. Consequently, the experiment demonstrates that, under the specific preregistered detectors and sample, no high-confidence contamination was observed and no guarded exclusions were applied; it does not establish that contamination is absent in other benchmarks, that other detectors would not flag items, nor that model memorization is generally negligible. Operational implication — auditors should: (a) ensure sampling from realistic, diverse, provenance-rich corpora; (b) prefer independent condition generations when measuring intervention effects unless shared generation semantics are specifically desired; (c) combine heuristic flags with manual adjudication or stronger provenance evidence to detect subtle contamination. Relation to prior work — our audit operationalizes contamination-detection recommendations from evaluation‑validity surveys and complements benchmarks that focus on repair efficacy by interrogating dataset integrity.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired audit of contamination-control effects in LLM-for-NetOps benchmarks and obtained a null confirmatory result (no change in validator pass rates). The null outcome arises from zero high-confidence contamination flags and shared-initial generation semantics. This result is scientifically informative: it documents a reproducible instance where preregistered heuristics and deterministic validators yield identical baseline and guarded outcomes, and it clarifies methodological choices that limit an audit's sensitivity. Future audits aiming to bound contamination impact should (i) sample provenance-rich, heterogeneous real-world items, (ii) use independent-condition generation or ensure guarded replacements occur, (iii) evaluate multiple models and detector thresholds, and (iv) combine automated flags with human adjudication when possible. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are supplied with the manuscript bundle for verification and reuse.

limitations: Single-model execution (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across other LLM families or sizes.

Sampled items were synthetic/deterministically generated for this run (source_identifier entries like synthetic-netops:task-XXXXX); absence of high-confidence flags may not reflect contamination prevalence in real-world, web-crawled benchmarks.

Generation semantics used shared_initial_candidate across baseline and guarded conditions (independent_condition_generation=false per preregistration), which produced identical model outputs when no exclusions occurred and therefore limited sensitivity to interventions that rely on independent re-generation.

Contamination detection relied on preregistered heuristic thresholds (exact-match and fuzzy 5-gram overlap); these heuristics are conservative and may miss subtler contamination patterns requiring richer provenance or manual adjudication.

Operational conclusions are bounded: a null paired effect here does not prove lack of contamination in other benchmarks, or that different detector definitions, sampling frames, or multi-model designs would yield similar results.

The validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) assesses a specified class of functional properties; passing that validator does not imply comprehensive production safety or absence of subtle semantic regressions outside the validator's checks.
